issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect the Developer initializer to accept an optional Int (monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int?). The template declares init(name: String, monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int?) but the solution implementation declares init(name: String, monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int) (non-optional). This conflicts with the client code in the solution which calls Developer(..., monthsOfSwiftExperience: nil). As written, the solution's initializer signature does not accept nil and would not compile with the client usage. This mismatch creates a structural inconsistency students could not reconcile when comparing the example solution and the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's Developer initializer parameter optional to match the specification and the template: change the signature to init(name: String, monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int?). Assign the parameter directly to the optional property (self.monthsOfSwiftExperience = monthsOfSwiftExperience). This will allow calls that pass nil (as in the client) and align the solution with the exercise description.
